clue.text: Was inclined, having served clumsily, to withdraw quietly

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull out, so the letter named alongside is taken away

blocks.note: to slop food is to serve it messily, spilling it
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone who felt like slipping away after making a mess of dishing up dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOPPED loses one P to give SLOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloped means leaned or slanted, the past tense of being inclined at an angle.

clue.text: Not a very busy period, but one gets a long way

blocks.note: first meaning: read as two words, a year whose workload is not heavy
second meaning: the astronomical unit, the vast distance light travels in a year

explanation.surface: A quiet spell at work that nonetheless sees someone make great progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LIGHT YEAR it is an easy year; as one term it is a measure of distance, not time, which is what makes the second half fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A light year is a unit of astronomical distance, roughly six trillion miles, so one of them covers a huge stretch.

clue.text: Clergyman even a little early?

blocks.note: surface reading: a churchman who turns up slightly ahead of time
setter's reading: split the answer into a prefix meaning before and a word meaning tardy, so it means before being tardy

explanation.surface: A churchman who is, for once, slightly ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PRE-LATE, the bishop's title becomes 'before late', which is what early means.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop or archbishop, so it names a clergyman.

clue.text: Perhaps man in Cardiff finds platform short

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a dais is a raised platform in a hall

explanation.surface: A Welshman comes across a stage that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: DAIS loses its S. DAI is a stock Welsh man's name, and Cardiff is the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai, a pet form of David, is the archetypal Welsh first name, so it is an example of a man from Wales.

clue.text: Recover from exercise, with fingers at side?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
with your fingers by your side, your arm hangs down

explanation.surface: Advice on relaxing after a workout by letting your hands hang loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a description, not a dictionary phrase: W plus ARM DOWN gives WARM DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-down is the gentle stretching done after sport to let the body return to rest.

clue.text: Carries on making money

blocks.note: first meaning: as in ... a war or campaign, keeps it going
second meaning: the pay someone earns from a job

explanation.surface: Someone continues working to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage is to conduct or pursue something such as war, and wages are the regular earnings paid for work.

clue.text: Prompt attention secures fibres for such clothes

blocks.note: prompt in the sense of quick and willing
tow is the coarse fibre of flax or hemp
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Quick attention to detail keeps the threads in place for a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secures' just joins the fibres to the attention; the definition 'such clothes' refers back to the whole description.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothes are mass-produced in standard sizes rather than made to measure, sold off the peg.

clue.text: Almost rainless? Nothing much more than that

definitions.text: Almost rainless? Nothing much more than that

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: rainless weather is dry
ought is an old form of nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that conditions are barely rainless and that is about all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a period much drier than merely almost rainless.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long spell with little or no rainfall, a step beyond weather that is merely dry.

clue.text: Thoroughly comfy to the end in wet-weather gear

indicators.note: going to the end of a word points at its last letter only

blocks.note: well can mean fully, as in well cooked
only the final letter of comfy is kept

explanation.surface: Being completely cosy while dressed for the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: A welly is short for a wellington, the British name for a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellies are waterproof rubber boots worn in rain and mud, so one is an item of wet-weather clothing.

clue.text: At one, no time for a welcome

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter named next is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a greeting is a welcome
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: No time for pleasantries at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one' looks like a time of day, which suits the surface's rush; it means in harmony. A followed by GREETING without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are at one are in agreement, so agreeing captures the same harmony of opinion.

clue.text: Divine figure with a halo on head?

blocks.note: taken as written
the poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax
a halo is a ring, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A painted god pictured with a ring of light above his head.
explanation.walkthrough: The halo O sits on the head POLL, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the Greek and Roman god of the sun, music and poetry, a deity.

clue.text: Russian navy skirts disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A news story about the Russian fleet narrowly avoiding catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian navy' reads as one phrase, but Russian alone is the definition and 'skirts' is fodder, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky, composer of The Rite of Spring, was born in Russia, so he is one Russian.

clue.text: Aim to tour round part of Parthenon, having lots of equipment

indicators.note: touring takes the front letter round to the back, so the word's first letter moves to its end
going round something encloses it, so the second piece sits inside the first

blocks.note: taken as written
the pediment is the triangular gable at each end of the Greek temple

explanation.surface: A tourist party lugging heavy kit around the Acropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: The pediment is the triangular gable over a Greek temple's columns; the 'tour' moves the first letter to the back before the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta is a formal word for baggage and equipment that slows travel, from the Latin for hindrances.

clue.text: No Jew — a painter

blocks.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement about an artist's religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double service in the surface but is a letter in the answer, leaving 'painter' as the definition with its article.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish artist, famous for The Third of May 1808, so he is one painter.

clue.text: The end of epoch before present

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of epoch
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A historian notes how an era ended just before our own time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like the noun for now, but the definition is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is present is here, in this place, as when answering a register.

clue.text: Point of card game, not on line — employing memory

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is taken out
to employ something is to take it on board, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: pontoon is the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack
taken as written; this is what is removed
RY, railway, is a common abbreviation for a line
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A query about scoring in a card game played offline using recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a score in the game but is a headland. The game loses its second on, a railway abbreviation is added, and computer memory slips in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland jutting into the sea, and a point is another word for such a headland.

clue.text: Allow, at this moment, head to drop

indicators.note: a head that drops falls to the bottom, so the first letter moves to the end of this down entry

blocks.note: now means at this moment

explanation.surface: Permitting someone to lower their head right now.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first letter is the top; N falls to the bottom of NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To own can mean to admit or concede, as in owning that someone is right, which is to allow it.

clue.text: Orders at intervals to take time-critical back up

indicators.note: taking things at intervals means every other one, so alternate letters are used

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of orders
something urgent must be done without delay

explanation.surface: Instructions to restore deadline-sensitive data from a backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' suggests copying computer files; here it means up again, rising once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising again after a decline, back up on its feet.

clue.text: I had travelled through French region to capital

indicators.note: travelling through a place means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
Provence is the region of south-east France

explanation.surface: A traveller describes crossing southern France on the way to a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is not Paris but an American state capital: PROV-ID-ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of the US state of Rhode Island.

clue.text: Casting an eye over contest — good to secure victory

blocks.note: to vie is to compete
a win is a victory
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A spectator watching a match, hoping the good side clinches it.
explanation.walkthrough: The good G is fastened on after the win.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing something is looking at or inspecting it, which is what casting an eye over means.

clue.text: Unable to move with speed

blocks.note: first meaning: stuck firmly
second meaning: quickly

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a spot from which they cannot get away quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly fixed, as in stuck fast, and rapid, its two opposite senses.

clue.text: Seeing political dissenters, fine to start shooting

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a film director calls action to start the cameras rolling

explanation.surface: A film crew spots a band of rebels and is cleared to start filming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming, and 'Action!' is the director's word to begin. 'Seeing' only leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group within a political party, a breakaway clique.

clue.text: Near avoiding cold, but go down

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: close means near
C is the tap marking for cold

explanation.surface: Getting close to victory without a chill, yet still falling short.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOSE without C.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down is to be defeated in a contest, which is what losing means.

clue.text: Window that's in airport not closed

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a word left open is not closed off, so it loses its final letter

blocks.note: Orly is one of the airports of Paris
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A traveller notes a window in a terminal that has been left open.
explanation.walkthrough: Orly is a Paris airport; 'not closed' leaves it open-ended by cutting its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey, supported on brackets.

clue.text: Scrooge for one I rope into support for prayer

blocks.note: Ebenezer Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the classic miser
taken as written
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: Tying the old skinflint up and leaving him with something to pray on.
explanation.walkthrough: A misericord is the small ledge on the underside of a hinged choir-stall seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A misericord let clergy lean while appearing to stand during long services, so it propped them up at prayer.

clue.text: One hunted by sailors in tin vessel

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Noah's ark is the vessel

explanation.surface: Seamen chase their quarry aboard a metal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark, whose hunters set sail on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Snark is the imaginary creature pursued by a ship's crew in Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem.

clue.text: Skimpily-dressed servant?

blocks.note: with a very short skirt on, read as two words: the skirt, then on

explanation.surface: A household attendant in a scanty uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split: MINI ON, someone with a miniskirt on, makes one word for a fawning servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a servile follower or underling who does a superior's bidding.

clue.text: Revolutionary causes securing good patronage

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the order of things, so these letters are rearranged
securing something means holding it fast inside, so the next piece is enclosed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: Radical movements winning the backing of a benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary causes' reads as political movements; Revolutionary is the anagram signal and causes the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their sponsorship and protection, which is patronage.

clue.text: Uncle deleting page from contents of in-box?

indicators.note: deleting is removing, so the named letter is cut out

blocks.note: spam is the junk email that fills an inbox
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A relative clearing out the emails in their inbox.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAM without its P. Uncle Sam is the personification of the US government.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the figure standing for the United States, so Sam is the uncle in question.

clue.text: Severe criticism about relative status in fleet

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: flak is harsh criticism, from anti-aircraft fire
gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Sharp words over a family member's standing in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: FLA-GRAN-K.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag rank is the grade of admiral, an officer entitled to fly a flag, so it is a status in a navy.

clue.text: Four different notes, or one official one

blocks.note: MI and UT are sol-fa names, E is a letter-named note and N abbreviates note, four kinds

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat weighing several jottings against one formal memo.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the old name for doh in sol-fa singing; MI-N-UT-E. 'One' in the definition stands for note.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a formal written note or memorandum, and minutes are the official record of a meeting.
